text.p: The exposure draft legislation for industry arrangements post-1997 clearly indicates the need for a well planned and managed transition from the present regulatory regime.
Some of the key areas of the transition include:
- The need to establish a number of industry bodies to implement a greater level of industry self-regulation.
- Preparation for the new access and interconnection arrangements
- Preparation for enhanced consumer protection provisions.
- Transfer of the competition functions to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).
- The merger of AUSTEL and Spectrum Management Authority (SMA).
All of these matters involve a significant lead time if they are to be in place and working by July 1, 1997.
This means that all industry stakeholders must begin contribuing to the transition as soon as possible if the new arrangements are to operate smoothly from July 1, 1997.
AUSTEL is committed to contributing wherever possible to this objective. However, we are also responsible for continuing to administer the current regulatory arrangements through to June 30, 1997.

These dual requirements will place a considerable strain on AUSTEL's resources in the months ahead. Accordingly, AUSTEL will be seeking to receive the utmost support from industry stakeholders during this critical period.
The post 1997 arrangements present an opportunity for unrestricted market entry with all suppliers competing under non-discriminatory terms and conditions.
The potential benefits for consumers from these new arrangements include better products, prices and performance.
How quickly the industry is able to grasp these opportunities will depend on how well we manage the transition to the post-1997 arrangements.
(The views are those of the author, not those of Reuters)
